pages.headline: Three questions this report answers
cards: How fast are EV sales growing?

pages.headline: Contents
items: Opportunity - where the next decade is won

pages.title: Market & momentum
pages.subtitle: Size, growth and the regional landscape
pages.takeaway: Growth is structural, but the next leg depends on affordability and charging.

pages.title: Demand keeps climbing as cheaper models arrive, but growth is cooling
body: Global electric-car sales rose from ~10m (2022) to ~17m (2025E) as cheaper models broadened the market.
Year-on-year growth eased from over 50% to the low-20s - a maturing, not stalling, market.
For a challenger, the prize shifts from being early to being cost-competitive at volume.

pages.title: Sales stay concentrated in three blocs, each on a different driver
body: China, Europe and North America take the large majority of global EV sales; China alone is more than half.
Each runs on a different driver.
Cost parity, emissions mandates and tax credits respectively - so a copy-paste strategy fails.
Sequence market entry by driver-fit, not by size alone.

pages.title: Two archetypes lead: integration vs cost leadership
pages.takeaway: Don't straddle. Win one lane, reach scale, then extend - margin follows focus.

pages.title: Four structural drivers keep compounding while subsidy fades
blocks: Adoption is pushed by falling battery cost, wider model choice, tighter emissions policy and better charging.
The first four are structural; subsidy was always transitional - growth after it is removed proves real demand.
Build the case on cost, product and policy - treat any incentive as upside, not foundation.

pages.headline: Back to the three questions - our view
lines: Growth is real but maturing - plan for a mainstream market by 2030.
Two models win - a challenger must pick one lane, not straddle both.
Opportunity is below and around the vehicle - affordability, software, supply.
So what: choose one spearhead lane, secure its scarce input, win a few markets first.

Approach: Layered desk research - facts, then insights, then implications; every figure traceable
Notes: All figures rounded / illustrative for a public demo - validate against primary sources
